_readme: PROVISIONING settings for the combined TST/ACC environment (Test and Acceptance
are one environment for this feature — TAD ADR-006). The provisioning scripts take
-Env <dev|test|acc|prd>; `test` IS TST/ACC here and `acc` is never used, so this is
the file every `-Env test` call in config/revitalise-grant-automation-pipeline.yml
resolves to.
This is NOT the pac import settings file. Two different kinds of settings file live
in this folder and they are consumed by different tools:
• <env>-settings.json  (this file) — read by the PowerShell scripts in
provisioning/ via Get-ProvisioningSettings. Describes Entra groups, Dataverse
group teams, role bindings, auditing, retention jobs and setting rows.
• pac-import-tstacc.json / pac-import-prd.json — passed to
`pac solution import --settings-file`. Supplies environment variable VALUES and
connection reference bindings at solution import time. Nothing else.
Identifiers only — never a secret, token or connection string (C-TECH-001). The
provisioning app id and certificate thumbprint stay in the environment variables
named under 'auth' (CI secrets / Key Vault).
Every {{PLACEHOLDER}} must be replaced with the real per-environment value before
the pipeline runs: Get-Setting fails fast on any value that still contains {{...}}
(C-TECH-031 / C-TECH-047). Values that are POLICY rather than per-environment
(retention periods, audit retention days, the fixed scoring maps) are real values
here by design — they must be identical in every environment.

entra._comment: Phase 1 groups only. rev-Finance-* and rev-Trustees-* are NOT created in this phase: no Phase 1 table is reachable by either persona. Group MEMBERSHIP is owned by the business/IAM process, never by the pipeline.
_comment_appRegistrations: App registrations are TENANT level, not per environment, so this block is IDENTICAL in
test-settings.json and prd-settings.json. That is deliberate and is the pattern
provisioning/README.md describes: run ensure-app-registration.ps1 once per settings file,
and idempotency makes the second run report EXISTS rather than creating a duplicate.
What IS per environment is the Dataverse application user, created by
PERMISSION IDS ARE {{PLACEHOLDER}} TOKENS ON PURPOSE, matching
dev-settings.example.json. The app-role GUIDs are stable across tenants but they are not
written here from memory: an incorrect GUID would grant a permission nobody reviewed.
Look each one up in the tenant (Graph: `GET /servicePrincipals(appId=...)?$select=appRoles`)
and paste it in. Every script fails fast while a token remains (C-TECH-047), so this
Least privilege is justified in TAD section 6.7 and ADR-018 (C-TECH-043):
Sites.Selected instead of Sites.FullControl.All, and Group.Create +
GroupMember.ReadWrite.All is tenant-wide and is the narrowest permission that can manage
group membership - which is why ADR-018 justifies it explicitly rather than assuming it.

appRegistrations._comment: THE TST/ACC DEPLOY IDENTITY, AND ONLY TST/ACC. Renamed and split from the former single shared `rev-grantautomation-deploy` on 2026-08-12 (ADR-007). Solution import/export and Power Platform Pipelines promotion into TST/ACC. Its authority in Dataverse comes from an APPLICATION USER IN TST/ACC ONLY, holding a least-privilege deployment role - NOT System Administrator, and not a broad API permission (TAD section 6.7). It must NOT be given an application user in PRD: that absence is the boundary.
appRegistrations._comment_why_split: Scoping several federated credentials onto ONE app registration would gate token ISSUANCE but not AUTHORITY - every subject would still resolve to a single service principal that is an application user in every environment, so a token minted by the tst_acc CI job could import into PRD. Splitting the registration moves the boundary to 'this identity does not exist in PRD at all', which is what C-TECH-043 least privilege asks for. Cost: this appRegistrations block is no longer identical to prd-settings.json - see config/revitalise-grant-automation-pipeline.yml tenant_prerequisites.

requiredResourceAccess._comment: Dataverse / Dynamics CRM. Scope user_impersonation, per TAD section 6.7.

resourceAccess._comment: Permission: user_impersonation (delegated Scope). Look up the id on the Dataverse service principal.

federatedCredentials._comment: C-TECH-044 RESOLVED 2026-08-12 - this credential is now the one actually in use, and no client secret exists on this registration. .github/workflows/ci.yml authenticates with `pac auth create --githubFederated`, which needs only the application id and tenant id.
federatedCredentials._comment_subject: THE SUBJECT IS THE GITHUB ENVIRONMENT, NOT A BRANCH. GitHub's OIDC `sub` claim is `repo:ORG/REPO:environment:NAME` for any job that references an environment, and only `repo:ORG/REPO:ref:refs/heads/BRANCH` for one that does not (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/oidc). Entra matches subjects as EXACT STRINGS with no wildcards. The previous value here was `ref:refs/heads/main`, which would never have matched: this workflow triggers on `feature/**`, so a branch subject would need one credential per branch name. Every authenticating job in ci.yml therefore declares an `environment:`, giving this one fixed subject per identity. EXACTLY ONE credential belongs on this registration - adding a second subject here would re-open the hole that splitting the registrations closed.
federatedCredentials.name: github-actions-env-tst-acc
federatedCredentials.subject: repo:{{GITHUB_ORG}}/{{GITHUB_REPO}}:environment:tst_acc

appRegistrations._comment: Signed with the certificate at PROVISION_CERT_THUMBPRINT (C-TECH-044). Original scope was Entra group creation, but ALL Phase 1 Entra groups (environment gates + persona/role groups) ended up created manually by the reviewer throughout this engagement — see test-settings.json's own group entries below, each annotated 'already created manually'. As of 2026-08-14 the reviewer confirmed they cannot grant admin consent for Microsoft Graph application permissions on this tenant (role limitation, not a preference), so the Group.Create / GroupMember.ReadWrite.All permission block that used to sit here was REMOVED rather than left unconsentable and unused (least privilege, C-TECH-043 — don't request a permission nothing exercises). If a later phase needs scripted group creation after all, the permission block that was here is preserved in git history (see the commit that removed it) rather than re-derived from memory.
appRegistrations._comment_dataverse: The Dataverse permission below is what this registration is actually used for now: ensure-schema.ps1 (provisioning/dataverse/) authenticates with this SAME PROVISION_APP_ID/PROVISION_CERT_THUMBPRINT credential to call the Dataverse Web API metadata endpoints. Mirrors the Dataverse permission block already declared on the rev-grantautomation-deploy-* registrations below: 'Dynamics CRM' only ever exposes ONE permission, user_impersonation, shown as a Delegated Scope in the Entra portal even when it backs an app-only client-credentials grant — there is no separate Application-type Dataverse permission to request. Consenting this scope is necessary but not sufficient: the app ALSO needs a Dataverse Application User in the target environment with a role capable of metadata operations (System Administrator or System Customizer — not a plain custom role, since CreateEntityRequest/CreateAttributeRequest-equivalent Web API calls aren't covered by the custom-privilege model at all). CONFIRMED WORKING 2026-08-14: live WhoAmI call against DEV succeeded once the application user was added there.

requiredResourceAccess._comment: SharePoint Online. Sites.Selected, chosen specifically to avoid Sites.FullControl.All (ADR-018). Scoped to /sites/grants when that site is created. Retained despite the Graph-consent limitation noted above because it is a DIFFERENT resource (SharePoint, not Graph) — consent for this one has not yet been attempted.
Dataverse / Dynamics CRM — ADDED 2026-08-14 for ensure-schema.ps1. Same resourceAppId and permission as the rev-grantautomation-deploy-* registrations.

resourceAccess._comment: Permission: user_impersonation (delegated Scope) — the only Dataverse permission that exists; used here to back an app-only client-credentials grant, same as the deploy identities.

appRegistrations._comment: ALEX'S WORDPRESS SITE AS AN OAUTH CLIENT-CREDENTIALS CALLER, and the identity the PRIMARY authentication control on the intake endpoint is built around (NFR-008, C-TECH-006). Created by provisioning/entra/ensure-intake-client.ps1, which also PRINTS the two identifiers the control needs: the application (client) id goes into the rev_IntakeAllowedClientId environment variable (the flow's second gate) and the SERVICE PRINCIPAL OBJECT ID goes into the trigger's 'Allowed users' field (the platform-level primary gate). They are different values and are not interchangeable.
appRegistrations._comment_adr011: ADR-011 IS STILL OPEN. This registration is the DEFAULT implementation, not the closed decision: the Entra OAuth route is now fully provisioned and testable, and the final intake channel choice is pending the conversation with Alex (the website developer). If that conversation lands on the shared-secret route or on the scheduled REST-pull route, DELETE this entry, the `intake` block below, provisioning/entra/ensure-intake-client.ps1 and provisioning/entra/verify-intake-endpoint-auth.ps1 together - leaving any of them behind creates an unused identity in the tenant and a smoke test that guards nothing. Dev Summary section 7, decision D-1.
appRegistrations._comment_credential: THE CALLER'S OWN CLIENT CREDENTIAL IS NOT PROVISIONED HERE AND IS NOT IN THIS REPOSITORY. Alex's site needs a certificate (preferred, C-TECH-044) or a client secret to obtain a token; it is issued interactively by the tenant administrator and handed over out of band. A pipeline that mints a credential is a pipeline that prints one (C-TECH-001). ensure-intake-client.ps1 reports whether one exists, by COUNT only.

requiredResourceAccess._comment: MICROSOFT FLOW SERVICE (Power Automate). Required so that Entra will issue this app a token whose aud claim is the Power Automate audience - without a declared permission on this resource, a client-credentials request for https://service.flow.microsoft.com//.default is refused and the endpoint cannot be called at all.
requiredResourceAccess._comment_lookup: PLACEHOLDER ON PURPOSE, per the block header above - not written from memory. Resolve both values in the tenant: `GET /servicePrincipals?$filter=displayName eq 'Microsoft Flow Service'&$select=appId,oauth2PermissionScopes`. The appId is commonly published as 7df0a125-d3be-4c96-aa54-591f83ff541c - CONFIRM that against the tenant rather than trusting it, then paste. The scope to take is the one named `User`.

resourceAccess._comment: Permission: User (delegated Scope) on Microsoft Flow Service. ⚠ ONE ITEM TO CONFIRM ON FIRST RUN: every published walkthrough of this pattern declares the DELEGATED `User` scope and then acquires an APP-ONLY token with `.default`, which is an unusual combination. If Entra refuses the client-credentials request, the fix is to grant the equivalent APPLICATION permission on the same resource and change `type` here to `Role`. Recorded rather than assumed - do not discover this in PRD.

_comment: THE PRIMARY AUTHENTICATION CONTROL ON THE SOLUTION'S ONE PUBLIC ENDPOINT
(NFR-008, C-TECH-006). Added 2026-08-12 to close test-agent defect D-001, which
found that the control the design calls 'the primary control' existed nowhere in
the delivery chain: not in the flow source, not in a provisioning script, not a
TAD §12 row, not a post_deploy step and not asserted by any smoke test.
IT IS A TRIGGER SETTING, NOT A SOLUTION COMPONENT. Microsoft documents it as the
'Who can trigger the flow?' authentication parameter on the 'When an HTTP request
is received' trigger and publishes no workflow-definition property for it
(https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/oauth-authentication). So it
cannot ship in the managed solution and cannot be asserted by reading the flow
JSON. It is therefore handled the only way such a control can be: declared here
as a value, applied by a NAMED OWNER as a post_deploy step, and VERIFIED after
every deployment by provisioning/entra/verify-intake-endpoint-auth.ps1.
WHETHER THE SETTING SURVIVES A SOLUTION IMPORT IS UNVERIFIED — there is no
environment yet. The pipeline therefore CONFIGURES IT AND VERIFIES IT on every
deployment rather than assuming it carried across. If it turns out to survive,
the post_deploy step becomes a no-op confirmation and the smoke test still earns
its place.
ADR-011 remains OPEN: this is the default implementation, not the settled
channel choice. See the _comment_adr011 note on the rev-wordpress-intake
registration above for what to delete if the decision lands elsewhere.

triggerAuthentication._comment_mode: The three documented modes are 'Any user in my tenant', 'Specific users in my tenant' and 'Anyone'. 'Anyone' is a defect. 'Any user in my tenant' would let ANY identity in the Revitalise tenant write applications into Dataverse, which is not least privilege for a single external caller. 'Specific users in my tenant' with one service principal object id is the narrowest available option and is what NFR-008 ('only the charity website') actually means. ⚠ Leaving the Allowed users field BLANK under this mode silently widens the scope back to the whole tenant, per Microsoft's own note — the smoke test cannot detect that, so it is called out here.
triggerAuthentication.allowedCallerSource: Service principal OBJECT id of intake.clientAppDisplayName — printed by provisioning/entra/ensure-intake-client.ps1. Not the application (client) id, and not the App-registrations Object ID: the Enterprise-applications one.
triggerAuthentication._comment_scope: Public-cloud values, and both are exact-match sensitive: the aud claim keeps its trailing slash, and the client-credentials scope therefore carries a DOUBLE slash before .default. A single slash yields a MisMatchingOAuthClaims failure that reads like a permissions problem and is not one.
triggerAuthentication.configuredBy: Wanstor (tenant administration) applies it in the Power Automate designer for the TST/ACC environment; Xander Lykopoulos (maker / Argelis Consultancy) supplies the service principal object id from the ensure-intake-client.ps1 output and confirms the smoke test passes. Recorded per C-TECH-041 so the control has a named owner, which is what D-001 found missing.

intake._comment_endpointUrl: THE TRIGGER URL IS A CREDENTIAL AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT A VALUE IN THIS FILE. A Power Automate HTTP trigger URL carries its own SAS signature in the `sig=` query parameter — Microsoft documents regenerating it (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/regenerate-sas-key), which is only meaningful for a secret. It is held as a CI secret under this name, like PROVISION_APP_ID (C-TECH-001/047). Read it once from the trigger card after the flow is turned on.

dataverse._comment_environmentUrl: The pipeline's $ENV_URL_TEST — one value for the combined TST/ACC environment (ADR-006). Environment REV-GrantApplications-ACC, created 2026-08-14, confirmed via `pac admin list` and now a Managed Environment (protection-level Standard, set 2026-08-14).

columnSecurityProfiles.name: REV_TrusteeRestricted
columnSecurityProfiles._comment: The profile ships in the managed solution; only its membership is provisioned. These two teams are the only principals that may read or write the Tier 4 secured columns (TAD §6, NFR-001).

auditing._comment: 6 years = 2192 days (C-DOM-010, C-DOM-011, TAD §6.5). A longer period — and -1, retain forever — would keep applicant data in audit history after the record itself was deleted, so this number is reviewed with the DPO, not defaulted in code.

bulkDeleteJobs.name: REV Retention - Rejected Applications
bulkDeleteJobs.description: Deletes applications with status Rejected once rev_decisiondate is older than 12 months (C-DOM-003, ADR-004).

bulkDeleteJobs.name: REV Retention - Withdrawn or Incomplete Applications
bulkDeleteJobs.description: Deletes applications with status Withdrawn or Incomplete once the parent applicant's rev_lastcontactdate is older than 6 months (C-DOM-003, ADR-004).

bulkDeleteJobs.name: REV Retention - Orphaned Applicants
bulkDeleteJobs._comment: No retention period of its own: an applicant with no remaining application inherits the period of whichever job deleted the last child. Runs after the two application sweeps (TAD §3.4 gap 1).
bulkDeleteJobs.description: Deletes applicant records that have no remaining child application — the derived orphan sweep.

bulkDeleteJobs.name: REV Retention - Error Log
bulkDeleteJobs.description: Deletes error log rows once rev_occurredon is older than 90 days. Error rows contain no personal data (C-DOM-004).

settingRows.description: Maps a wellbeing answer's option VALUE to circumstance points (FR-013). Position 1 scores 5, position 5 scores 1. Key "6" ('Not sure') = 0, CHANGED FROM 0.5 on 2026-08-20 and confirmed with Emily (process owner). This supersedes the D-014 derivation from the hand-scored export; the map now holds no fractional value, so the half-point rounding can never fire. Full record: provisioning/deploymentSettings/settings-rows.notes.md#LikertPointMap.

Inverts the life-satisfaction answer rev_feelingscaleanswer, a whole number 0 to 10, so that a lower reported satisfaction scores more points (FR-012). This is 10 minus the raw answer, expressed as a lookup map so the direction of the scale is configuration rather than arithmetic inside the flow. REPLACED IN REVISION 0.3: it was a five-entry map over a five-option picklist. The Automation Solution Design v0.5 specifies exactly this for Automation #2 Q1 — "inverted (0/10 feeling = 10 points)".
Circumstance score at or below which the application status becomes Auto-reject. PROVISIONAL TEST VALUE in TST/ACC — the board's figure is SDD OQ-001.
Lower bound (inclusive) of the Borderline review band. PROVISIONAL TEST VALUE in TST/ACC — SDD OQ-002.
Upper bound (inclusive) of the Borderline review band; a score above it becomes Auto-pass. PROVISIONAL TEST VALUE in TST/ACC — SDD OQ-002.
Annual household income ceiling in GBP. PROVISIONAL TEST VALUE in TST/ACC — SDD OQ-003.

Maps an age in whole years to a rev_agerange option value (1=Under 18 .. 8=75 and over). Fixed reference data. Option 9 (Not known) is the fallback when no date of birth was supplied and is therefore not in the map.

Maps the age-band labels the live form actually sends to rev_agerange (2=18-24 .. 8=75+, 9=Not known). The live form asks an age band directly, NOT a date of birth, so this map — not AgeBandMap — is the primary route to rev_agerange. Matched case-insensitively after trimming. Option 1 (Under 18) has no label (form gates on 18+). Full derivation kept in provisioning/deploymentSettings/settings-rows.notes.md#AgeRangeLabelMap (D-021).

Matched case-insensitively after trimming. An unmatched label leaves the column empty rather than guessing - see rev_intakereviewnote. Full derivation: settings-rows.notes.md#ExceptionalCircumstanceLabelMap.

settingRows.description: Maps the employment-status labels the live form sends to rev_employmentstatus option values (FR-064, form-field-corrections pass). Matched case-insensitively after trimming. An unmatched label leaves the column empty rather than guessing. Full derivation: settings-rows.notes.md#EmploymentStatusLabelMap.

Maps the care-hours band labels the live form sends to rev_carehoursperweek option values (FR-064, form-field-corrections pass). Matched case- and dash-insensitively after trimming - the live form and other sources render band 2's dash differently. An unmatched label leaves the column empty. Full derivation: settings-rows.notes.md#CareHoursBandLabelMap.

Maps the uppercased alphabetic prefix of a UK outward code to a rev_locationarea option value (1=North East .. 12=Northern Ireland). Longest prefix wins, so match SW before S. Fixed reference data. Option 13 (Not known) is the fallback for an unrecognised or absent postcode and is therefore not in the map.

Maximum attainable circumstance score, for rendering 'n out of N': 10 wellbeing answers x 5 (50) plus the inverted life-satisfaction answer up to 10 = 60 (FR-011). Confirmed 60, not 55 — life-satisfaction is the 0-10 scale its source describes; matches the raw export header and Automation Solution Design v0.5. Unblocks KnockoutThreshold and the Borderline band (SDD OQ-001/002). Full derivation kept in provisioning/deploymentSettings/settings-rows.notes.md#MaxCircumstanceScore (D-021).

Maps each rev_incomeband option to the top of that band, compared against IncomeCeiling (FR-015). NFR-019: if the form's income bands change, this row changes, not the scoring flow. Option 5 (40,000+) is unbounded with a sentinel above any realistic ceiling; option 6 (Prefer not to say) carries -1, mapped to income flag 3, not a guess. Not pending — this is the option set's definition. Full derivation kept in provisioning/deploymentSettings/settings-rows.notes.md#IncomeBandUpperBoundMap (D-021).

_comment_omitted_blocks: No `sharepoint` and no `teams` block, deliberately. Phase 1 provisions no
SharePoint site (the four tables hold no documents — DocuSign and file storage are
later phases) and no Microsoft Team: the only Teams usage is a 1:1 chat
notification sent to the process owner through the Teams connector (TAD ADR-015),
which needs a connection reference in pac-import-tstacc.json, not a provisioned
team. There is also no `code` app entry — Phase 1 ships the model-driven app only.
The pipeline therefore calls no sharepoint/* or teams/* script.
